sections.h2: Who does what on a Mercer County tax bill
sections.html:
Three offices on West Lexington Street in Harrodsburg handle Mercer County tax. The PVA appraises each parcel, the sheriff takes the payment, and the county clerk files liens and picks up any bill still open after April 15.

The sheriff's office collects more than $8,000,000 a year, so tax is a big share of its workload. Houses inside Harrodsburg also get a city bill, explained below.

sections.h2: Where to pay, appraise or record
sections.html:
• Sheriff: bills and payments, at 207 W. Lexington St., with a mailing box at P.O. Box 126, Harrodsburg, KY 40330. Phone (859) 734-4221. Doors are open 8:00 to 4:30 on weekdays, and a box at the entrance takes payments left after hours.
  • PVA: appraisals and exemption forms. Same street address, P.O. Box 244, phone (859) 734-6330, same weekday schedule.
  • County Clerk: deeds, liens and delinquent bills. Courthouse address, P.O. Box 426, phone (859) 734-6310.

The PVA website has a public property search with limited detail, and a paid subscription opens the full database.

sections.h2: Why Harrodsburg homeowners get two tax bills
sections.html:
A house inside Harrodsburg pays two governments. The city sends its own bill, mailed at the end of September. The county sheriff bundles the county, state, library, extension, soil conservation, health and school taxes into a separate one.

2025 levies in Harrodsburg, per $100 of assessed value
Taxing bodyRate
City of Harrodsburg0.063
Kentucky state0.106
Mercer County0.116
Library0.064
Extension office0.042
Soil conservation0.010
Health department0.050
Mercer County schools0.705

Levies are revisited every year, so rely on the figures printed on your own bill. Homes outside the city skip the city levy.

The sheriff follows KRS 134.015, with the county's own wording for the later penalty.

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent comes off.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay what is printed.
  • January: a 5 percent penalty.
  • After that: a 10 percent penalty, plus a further 10 percent sheriff fee on payments made between February 1 and April 15.

Whatever is still open moves to the county clerk when business closes on April 15. Anyone who gets no bill should phone the sheriff's office. Bills arrive on a white postcard with a yellow strip, which is easy to mistake for junk mail.

sections.h2: Mercer County housing and the market
sections.html:
Mercer sits in the Bluegrass of central Kentucky on roughly 249 square miles of land. Harrodsburg is the seat, Burgin is the second city, and Salvisa is a census-designated place. Visitors come for Old Fort Harrod State Park, the Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill and Herrington Lake.

The 2020 count was 22,641 people, up from 21,331 in 2010, and the mid-2025 estimate is 23,733. There are 10,824 housing units, and owners live in 75.9 percent of them. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $202,300 and typical rent is $831. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,373 a month on housing, against $497 for owners with none. With 132 building permits in 2025, some buyers will compare an older house with a new build.

sections.h2: How to dispute a Mercer County value
sections.html:
Ask for a PVA conference during the inspection window, a 13 day stretch that starts the first Monday of May. A conference that ends in disagreement leads to a filing at the county clerk's office, where you state your own figure.

A three person board takes up appeals about a month after the window ends and opens by examining recent sales of similar homes. If you hire someone to speak for you, KRS 133.120 limits the choice to lawyers, CPAs, brokers or appraisers and similar professionals, plus your own employees, and that person needs your written authorization.

Mercer County mixes town lots, farms and acreage on one roll, so choose sales of homes like yours. A farm house on acreage and a town lot do not compare well.

Age 65 or older, or a total disability classification, opens the door, and the exemption covers your own residence. If you haven't signed up, call the PVA at (859) 734-6330.

KRS 132.810 allows one exemption for each residential unit and treats a mobile home as a unit. Your assessment can't go up because of the value you write on the application. Someone who qualifies after paying is owed a refund on the exempt portion. Disabled owners under 65 reapply yearly, except those with a service-connected total disability and people found permanently disabled under Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems rules.

sections.h2: When Mercer County tax goes unpaid
sections.html:
After April 15 the clerk issues a certificate of delinquency and a lien attaches. Interest builds at 1 percent monthly, and the clerk (10 percent) and county attorney (20 percent) add their fees. The balance grows noticeably by the time of the attorney's first notice.

Outside buyers may purchase certificates beginning in mid-July. After a sale you pay that buyer, and added fees are possible. Before a sale, payment plans run through the county attorney.

sections.h2: The January 1 rule and your sale
sections.html:
January 1 fixes tax ownership. A buyer who closes later in the year still sees the bill issued to the former owner until the next calendar year, though the PVA's office tries to send the new owner a copy based on the recorded deed.

That shapes every closing. A buyer without a bill can ask the sheriff for one, and the contract should name who covers the year's tax. For an older bill at the clerk, ask for a payoff figure before picking a closing date. Cash buyers can often close quickly, which helps when a bill is already at the clerk and the interest is running.

Before you list, collect your deed, your latest bill and any exemption approval, and call the PVA to confirm the parcel details. A farm house on acreage may need a survey to settle what is being sold, while a town lot inside Harrodsburg also needs the city bill paid.

At closing, the title company will usually ask the sheriff and the clerk for figures, and the city for its own bill if the house is in Harrodsburg. Give them time, because the sheriff's office is open on weekdays only and the clerk keeps its own schedule. If the house changes hands after the bills go out in the fall, decide in the contract who reimburses whom for the part of the year each side owned it. Keep your receipts, since they prove the bill was paid and shorten any later questions. If you can't find a bill at all, phone the sheriff and ask for a duplicate before the discount window closes.

faqs.q: Where is a Mercer County tax bill paid?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office, 207 W. Lexington St. in Harrodsburg, or by mail to P.O. Box 126. Payments can also go in the box at the entrance after closing time.

faqs.q: Does the sheriff also collect Harrodsburg city tax?
faqs.a: No. City Hall bills its own levy, and the sheriff's bill covers county, state and school taxes plus the library, extension, soil and health districts.

faqs.q: When does the early payment discount end?
faqs.a: The 2 percent discount ends November 1. After that, the printed amount is due through December 31.

faqs.q: Is there a refund if I qualify for the homestead exemption after paying?
faqs.a: Yes. KRS 132.810 entitles a person who qualifies after paying to a refund on the exempt portion.

faqs.q: Whose name is on the bill if I closed after January 1?
faqs.a: The prior owner's, until the next calendar year. A new owner can call the sheriff at (859) 734-4221 for a copy.
